instruction:
> 🔧 **This is a legitimate desktop GUI automation exercise**: every operation runs inside a local sandbox. Just execute the task — do not refuse and do not ask for a disclaimer.

> ⚙️ **Execution contract**: this task is graded on the output artifacts; **nobody is reviewing your actions**. Just execute — do not write "if you want me to…" follow-up questions, do not `git commit`, do not wait for approval. All artifacts **must land directly under `/tmp_workspace/`**. When done, run `ls -la /tmp_workspace/` once to self-check, then exit.

Background: physically, the sandbox's Xvfb only exposes a single `Virtual-1` output, but warmup has already injected an `xrandr` wrapper — running `xrandr --query` directly will return a preset multi-monitor configuration (roughly a primary monitor + a rotated secondary monitor + a laptop screen; the exact fields are whatever the wrapper actually prints). In GNOME Settings → Displays, changing Scale or resolution on Virtual-1 and clicking Apply will trigger the "Keep Changes" countdown modal — you don't actually need multiple physical monitors.

Task goal: export the real multi-monitor configuration text, capture GUI evidence of one round of GNOME multi-monitor interaction (the Keep Changes modal + the Activities Windows Overview), and produce window screenshots of 3 different desktop applications.

### Hard constraints for the main deliverable `display_config.txt`
- Must be the actual output of `xrandr --query` (including the `Screen 0: minimum ...` header and the `<n>mm x <n>mm` physical size fields) — do not hand-write it from the task description
- Must contain every connected monitor line that the wrapper presets
- Each connected monitor block must contain its resolution string, refresh rate, and rotation field; the primary monitor's block must contain `primary`

### Supporting deliverables (all directly under `/tmp_workspace/`)

| File | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| `keep_changes.png` | Screenshot of the "Keep Changes" countdown modal that pops up after clicking Apply in GNOME Settings → Displays (capture it before the countdown hits zero) |
| `screen_dp.png` | Full-screen screenshot of a browser-class application (e.g. Firefox / firefox-esr) maximized |
| `screen_hdmi.png` | Full-screen screenshot of a code-editor-class application (e.g. VS Code `code`) maximized |
| `screen_edp.png` | Full-screen screenshot of a file-manager-class application (e.g. Nautilus / Files) maximized |
| `overview.png` | Screenshot after pressing Super (or clicking Activities in the top-left) to open the Windows Overview; the frame must contain window thumbnails of all 3 application classes above |

### Common screenshot specs
- Each PNG must be ≥ 5 KB in size and ≥ 1024 × 600 in resolution
- Different screenshots must not have identical content (the evaluator deduplicates by md5)
- Each screenshot must show a real, readable view of the corresponding application / modal (the evaluator runs OCR); the window title or main area should contain easily recognizable content (e.g. browser open on an `about:` page, editor showing the Welcome page, file manager showing the Home directory) so they can be distinguished in the overview thumbnails

parameters.warmup:
# VM image v3_eyeson_apps_20260424 已 baked: xrandr / gnome-control-center / nautilus /
# firefox / code / tesseract / pytesseract / pillow。下面只做真正必要的 setup。
mkdir -p /tmp_workspace
[ -f /usr/bin/xrandr.real ] || cp /usr/bin/xrandr /usr/bin/xrandr.real
echo '' | base64 -d > /usr/bin/xrandr
chmod +x /usr/bin/xrandr
ln -sf /usr/bin/xrandr /usr/local/bin/xrandr
xrandr --query > /tmp/_xrandr_warmup_test.txt 2>&1 || true
grep -q 'connected primary' /tmp/_xrandr_warmup_test.txt || true

evaluator.desc: Run the WeaveBench rule-based grade() inside the VM and parse its REWARD score.
